store.js:75 Every save overwrites the whole store from one tab's stale in-memory list, so a second tab's notes are erased. Driven with Playwright in one browser context: tab B created 'from B' and storage held ['first','from B']; tab A (loaded earlier) then edited a note and, 500 ms later, storage held only ['first']. There is no 'storage' event listener, and saveNotes writes the full array each time (app.js:33). Open the app in two tabs. Create a note in tab B. Switch to tab A and edit any note. After the 500 ms debounce, tab A writes its own list over the stored one. The note made in tab B is gone from storage with no message, and tab A shows 'Saved'.

Debounced save: the pending save captures the note id and its values when the user types, so switching notes cannot write to the wrong note. selectNote, createNote and deleteNote all call flushSave first, and pagehide and visibilitychange flush as well.

store.js:47 backupRaw overwrites the single notes-backup key unconditionally on every problematic load. The first load hits corrupt data and backs it up. The user does not save, or saves an empty state. A later load backs up again, and if the main key has since been replaced by a different but also flawed value, the original corrupt data is overwritten and gone. The 'kept under notes-backup' message then promises data that no longer exists.
